projects.name: Analytics Dashboard
projects.description:
A new analytics dashboard project that ingests and processes customer CSV files, analyzes application log data, and presents insights through visualization components. Scope covers three major workstreams: (1) CSV data processing pipeline for customer data, (2) application log analysis and aggregation, and (3) dashboard visualization components and UI. Delivery will be structured as milestones broken into granular, executable tasks with explicit dependencies, complexity estimates, and verification criteria.

Tags: analytics, dashboard, data-engineering, visualization

tasks.name: M1: Foundation, Data Contracts & Scaffolding
tasks.details: Milestone 1. Establish the technical foundation before any pipeline work: repository/tooling scaffold, data source inventory, and agreed data contracts for both the customer CSV feed and the application log stream. Exit criteria: repo builds and runs tests in CI, CSV and log schemas are documented and validated against real sample files, and storage/layout conventions are agreed. All execution work is decomposed into child tasks of complexity 4 or below.

tasks.name: M2: Customer CSV Ingestion & Processing Pipeline
tasks.details: Milestone 2. Build the end-to-end pipeline that turns raw customer CSV exports into validated, deduplicated, query-ready customer records. Covers file intake, parsing, schema validation, cleansing/normalization, deduplication, and load into the analytics store with idempotency and audit logging. Exit criteria: a real customer CSV can be ingested repeatably with row-level rejects surfaced and no duplicate customer records. All execution work is decomposed into child tasks of complexity 4 or below.

tasks.name: M3: Application Log Analysis & Aggregation
tasks.details: Milestone 3. Build the log analytics pipeline that parses application logs, classifies severity and event types, and produces aggregated operational metrics (error rates, latency percentiles, top failure signatures, traffic trends). Exit criteria: logs for a full day can be processed end-to-end, error/latency metrics reconcile against a manual spot check, and aggregates are available for the dashboard's time-series endpoints. All execution work is decomposed into child tasks of complexity 4 or below.

tasks.name: M4: Metrics & Data Serving API
tasks.details: Milestone 4. Expose the processed customer and log data to the frontend through a stable, documented read API. Covers the analytic query layer, REST endpoints for each dashboard widget, filtering/pagination/time-range parameters, caching, and auth. Exit criteria: every planned dashboard widget has a corresponding documented endpoint returning correct data within latency targets. All execution work is decomposed into child tasks of complexity 4 or below.

tasks.name: M5: Dashboard Visualization Components & UI
tasks.details: Milestone 5. Build the user-facing dashboard: application shell and layout, a shared charting component library, and the individual widgets (customer analytics, operational health, log exploration) wired to the API. Exit criteria: dashboard renders all widgets with real data, is responsive, handles loading/empty/error states, and passes an accessibility review. All execution work is decomposed into child tasks of complexity 4 or below.

tasks.name: M6: Hardening, Documentation & Launch
tasks.details: Milestone 6. Make the system production-ready and launch it: performance and cost tuning, end-to-end testing, monitoring/alerting on pipeline freshness and error rates, operational runbooks, and staged rollout. Exit criteria: green E2E suite, documented runbooks, dashboards monitored in production, and sign-off for general availability. All execution work is decomposed into child tasks of complexity 4 or below.

tasks.name: Set up repository, tooling and CI scaffold
tasks.details: Sequence 1.1 (no prerequisites). Create the monorepo layout (backend, frontend, pipelines, shared schemas), pin runtime/linter/formatter versions, add Makefile or npm scripts for build/test/lint, and wire a CI workflow that runs lint + unit tests on every push. Verification: a trivial committed test runs green in CI from a clean clone.

tasks.name: Inventory data sources and collect representative samples
tasks.details: Sequence 1.2 (no prerequisites; can run parallel with 1.1). Enumerate every customer CSV export (who produces it, how often, column changes in last 6 months, known quirks) and every application log stream (files, services, volume/day, format). Collect 3-5 representative sample files including the largest and the messiest, and store them as sanitized fixtures with a documented provenance note. Verification: a source inventory table exists and every source has at least one checked-in sample.

tasks.name: Define customer CSV data contract and schema
tasks.details: Sequence 1.3 (requires 1.2). Specify the canonical customer record: each field's name, type, nullability, format/regex, allowed values, source column mapping, and PII classification. Document encoding/delimiter/quote rules, which columns are required vs best-effort, and the reject policy for invalid rows. Ship it as a machine-readable schema (e.g. JSON Schema/Pydantic) plus a human-readable doc. Verification: schema validates every collected sample and a peer review signs off.

tasks.name: Define application log data contract and parsed-event spec
tasks.details: Sequence 1.4 (requires 1.2). Specify the structured event model extracted from raw log lines: timestamp (with timezone rule), level, service, host, request id, route, status code, duration, message, stack/error signature, plus optional JSON payload fields. Include the parsing strategy per source, fallback for unparseable lines, severity mapping table, and PII redaction rules. Verification: spec covers 100% of distinct line shapes found in the samples, with each shape mapped to fields.

tasks.name: Define storage layout, naming conventions and environment config
tasks.details: Sequence 1.5 (requires 1.3 and 1.4 for column planning). Choose the analytics store and lay out raw/staging/curated zones, table and column naming, partition/clustering keys for time-series and customer data, retention, and environment config loading (dev/staging/prod) with secrets kept out of the repo. Verification: an ADR records the choice and trade-offs, and config templating boots locally with dummy values.

tasks.name: CSV file intake and staging manifest
tasks.details: Sequence 2.1 (requires 1.1 scaffold and 1.5 storage layout). Implement discovery of incoming customer CSV files (local drop folder or object-store prefix), compute checksum, write a manifest row per file (path, size, checksum, received_at, source), copy into the raw zone without mutation, and skip already-seen checksums. Verification: uploading the same file twice produces exactly one manifest entry and one raw object.

tasks.name: CSV parsing with dialect, encoding and header handling
tasks.details: Sequence 2.2 (requires 2.1 and 1.3 contract). Build the reader that detects/handles delimiter, quote char, BOM, encoding (UTF-8, Latin-1), embedded newlines, CRLF, header renames/case differences, and trailing empty columns; emit typed raw rows plus a per-file parse report (row count, malformed row numbers). Verification: parses every sample file including the deliberately messy fixture with zero crashes and correct row counts.

tasks.name: Row-level schema validation and reject handling
tasks.details: Sequence 2.3 (requires 2.2). Apply the 1.3 schema per row, collect all violations (not just the first), route invalid rows to a rejects table/CSV with row number plus failure reasons, and emit a validation summary with pass/fail/reject counts. Include a configurable policy for reject-on-error vs. quarantine-and-continue. Verification: a fixture with known bad rows yields exactly the expected reject records and reasons.

tasks.name: Field normalization and cleansing rules
tasks.details: Sequence 2.4 (requires 2.3). Implement canonicalization: trim/collapse whitespace, email lowercasing and validation, phone/E.164 and country/state normalization, date and currency parsing to ISO/typed values, boolean and enum coercion, empty-string-to-null, and deterministic handling of unknown enumerations. Keep the original raw value alongside the normalized value for auditability. Verification: a golden fixture table asserts before/after for every rule.

tasks.name: Customer deduplication and identity resolution
tasks.details: Sequence 2.5 (requires 2.4). Define the match key hierarchy (stable customer id, then normalized email, then fuzzy name+address fallback with a similarity threshold), assign a canonical customer_id, merge survivorship rules (most recent non-null per field), and record merge decisions in an auditable crosswalk table. Verification: a fixture with known duplicate pairs collapses to the expected single records and no false merges occur on the distinct-control set.

tasks.name: Idempotent upsert load into curated customer table
tasks.details: Sequence 2.6 (requires 2.5 and 1.5). Stage the cleansed records, then MERGE/upsert on canonical customer_id with change detection (updated_at, row hash) so nothing is duplicated and unchanged rows are not rewritten; support soft deletes for customers absent from a full snapshot. Wrap the load in a transaction or atomic table swap. Verification: running the same load twice leaves row counts and checksums identical.

tasks.name: CSV pipeline orchestration, run ledger and rerun support
tasks.details: Sequence 2.7 (requires 2.6). Chain the CSV steps into one runnable job with a run ledger (run_id, file, stage statuses, counts, duration, error), structured logs, retry/backoff on transient failures, a --dry-run mode, and a documented way to replay a specific file from raw. Verification: an intentionally induced mid-pipeline failure is retryable and the ledger shows exactly which stage failed.

tasks.name: CSV pipeline unit tests and fixture suite
tasks.details: Sequence 2.8 (write alongside 2.2-2.7, finalize last). Build pytest/unittest coverage for parsing, validation, normalization, dedupe, and idempotent load using checked-in sanitized fixtures; include regression fixtures for every bug found during the build and enforce a coverage floor in CI. Verification: suite runs green in CI and a deliberate mutation in a normalization rule fails a test.

tasks.name: Log ingestion adapter for rotated files and streams
tasks.details: Sequence 3.1 (requires 1.2 samples, 1.5 storage). Implement reading of application logs from rotated files (gzip/plain, date-suffixed naming) or a stream tail, tracking byte offsets/checkpoints per source so restarts do not re-read or skip lines, and landing raw batches in the raw zone with a batch manifest. Verification: restart mid-file resumes at the correct offset and a rotated/compressed file is read fully once.

tasks.name: Log line parsing and structured event extraction
tasks.details: Sequence 3.2 (requires 3.1 and 1.4 contract). Implement the parser(s) for each line format (plain text with regex, JSON lines, key=value), multi-line stack-trace aggregation into the parent event, and an unparsed-line bucket that preserves the raw text with a reason code. Emit typed event records matching the 1.4 spec plus per-batch parse statistics. Verification: parse-success rate on real samples is at least 99% and every unparsed line has a reason code.

tasks.name: Timestamp normalization and late-arrival handling
tasks.details: Sequence 3.3 (requires 3.2). Normalize all timestamps to UTC using the source's declared timezone or offset, handle missing/ambiguous timestamps by falling back to ingestion time with a flag, define event_time vs. ingest_time, and describe how late-arriving events are attributed to the correct hour bucket on reprocessing. Verification: a fixture spanning DST change and multiple offsets buckets into the expected UTC hours.

tasks.name: Severity and event-type classification rules
tasks.details: Sequence 3.4 (requires 3.2). Implement the severity mapping table from raw level strings (WARN/WARNING/warning, ERROR, FATAL vs. structured status codes) into a canonical enum, and derive event_type (http_request, db_query, job_run, auth, exception, etc.) from route/message patterns. Make rules data-driven in a config file so they can be tuned without code changes. Verification: a labeled set of 200 sampled lines classifies at 95%+ agreement with human labels.

tasks.name: Error signature fingerprinting and grouping
tasks.details: Sequence 3.5 (requires 3.4). Normalize error/exception messages (mask ids, numbers, UUIDs, quoted values, timestamps) to build a stable fingerprint per failure mode, keep an exemplar message and stack for each fingerprint, and count occurrences first_seen/last_seen. Verification: the same error with different ids collapses to one fingerprint while distinct error types stay separate, demonstrated on a fixture.

tasks.name: Latency, throughput and error-rate metric computation
tasks.details: Sequence 3.6 (requires 3.3 and 3.4). Compute per-window metrics: request count, error count and error rate (5xx and 4xx separately), p50/p90/p95/p99 latency from duration fields, requests-per-minute throughput, and slowest-route ranking. Document exact definitions and how non-request events are excluded. Verification: metric definitions match a hand-computed fixture to the exact value, and percentiles match an independent numpy reference.

tasks.name: Hourly and daily aggregation rollups with idempotent rebuild
tasks.details: Sequence 3.7 (requires 3.6). Persist hourly and daily rollup tables (metrics by service, route, severity, fingerprint) partitioned by date, with a deterministic overwrite-per-partition write so reruns never double count. Include a backfill command for a date range and a freshness marker per partition. Verification: rebuilding a day twice yields identical rollups, and a backfill of 7 days completes with correct totals.

tasks.name: PII redaction and retention enforcement in logs
tasks.details: Sequence 3.8 (requires 3.2). Apply redaction rules for emails, tokens/bearer headers, card-like numbers, IPs (if required) and user identifiers before persistence, plus a retention job that drops raw log partitions past the agreed window while keeping aggregates. Verification: a fixture containing each sensitive pattern shows zero unmasked values in curated output, and the retention job removes only partitions older than the policy.

tasks.name: Log pipeline tests and metric reconciliation check
tasks.details: Sequence 3.9 (write alongside 3.2-3.7, finalize last). Unit tests for parsers, classifiers, fingerprinting and metric math, plus an integration test that processes a full fixture day and reconciles total requests, error count and p95 latency against values computed independently (e.g. grep/awk or a notebook). Verification: tests green in CI and the reconciliation report is committed as an artifact.

tasks.name: Analytic query layer and data access modules
tasks.details: Sequence 4.1 (requires 2.6 customer table and 3.7 rollups). Build the service/repository layer that reads curated customer records and log rollups, applies date-range and dimension filters in SQL, and returns typed result objects. Keep SQL centralized here (no queries in route handlers) and parameterize everything. Verification: repository unit tests run against a seeded test database and return expected aggregates.

tasks.name: Widget-to-endpoint contract specification
tasks.details: Sequence 4.2 (do first in this milestone, before 4.3-4.5). For each planned dashboard widget, write the request (path, query params, filters, granularity) and the exact response JSON shape the frontend will consume, including units, null semantics and timezone. Agree this with the frontend owner so both sides build to the same document. Verification: every widget in the M5 list maps to one spec entry and the frontend sign-off is recorded.

tasks.name: Customer metrics and segment endpoints
tasks.details: Sequence 4.3 (requires 4.1 and 4.2). Implement endpoints for customer totals, new-customers-per-period, active/inactive split, geographic or plan distribution, and a paginated customer list with search and sort. Include input validation and consistent envelope/pagination metadata. Verification: endpoint tests assert values against seeded fixtures and reject invalid parameters with 400s.

tasks.name: Operational health time-series endpoints
tasks.details: Sequence 4.4 (requires 4.1 and 4.2). Implement endpoints for error-rate, request-volume, latency-percentile and top-error-signature series with from/to range, granularity (hour/day), service and route filters. Return gaps explicitly rather than interpolating silently. Verification: responses validated against fixture rollups for hour and day granularity, including a range with missing buckets.

tasks.name: Log search and explore endpoint with pagination
tasks.details: Sequence 4.5 (requires 4.1 and 4.2). Implement a filtered log-event search: free-text contains, severity, service, route, fingerprint, time range, with cursor or keyset pagination, bounded page size, total-count strategy, and a hard cap on scan range. Return redacted fields only. Verification: paging through a large fixture yields no duplicates or gaps and the max-range guard returns a clear 422.

tasks.name: Response caching and query performance guardrails
tasks.details: Sequence 4.6 (requires 4.3-4.5). Add a short-TTL cache for heavy dashboard queries keyed by normalized params, conditional requests or ETags, query timeouts, and index/partition verification for the top queries. Capture p95 endpoint latency before and after. Verification: repeated identical requests hit cache (measurable latency drop) and the slowest endpoint meets the agreed p95 target on production-sized data.

tasks.name: API authentication, authorization and rate limiting
tasks.details: Sequence 4.7 (requires 4.3-4.5). Add authentication for dashboard clients (session or JWT), role-based access so only authorized users see customer PII fields, rate limiting per client, CORS policy, and audit logging of sensitive reads. Verification: unauthenticated calls get 401, under-privileged calls get 403 with PII fields stripped, and exceeding the rate limit returns 429.

tasks.name: OpenAPI documentation and API contract tests
tasks.details: Sequence 4.8 (last in this milestone). Publish an OpenAPI spec covering every endpoint with example payloads, define the standard error envelope (code, message, details), and add contract tests that fail if a response shape drifts from 4.2. Provide a seed script so a developer can run the API locally with demo data. Verification: spec renders, contract tests pass, and a new developer can boot the API with seeded data following only the README.

tasks.name: Frontend application shell, routing and layout
tasks.details: Sequence 5.1 (requires 1.1 scaffold). Scaffold the frontend app, set up routing for the dashboard pages (overview, customers, operations/logs), the top-level layout with nav/sidebar/header and a placeholder page per route. Verification: app builds, every route renders its placeholder, and deep links work on refresh.

tasks.name: Design tokens, theming and responsive dashboard grid
tasks.details: Sequence 5.2 (requires 5.1). Define color/typography/spacing tokens and a categorical palette that is colorblind-safe, a light/dark theme switch, and a 12-column responsive grid with breakpoints for desktop/tablet/mobile that widget cards snap into. Verification: a gallery page shows tokens and grid breakpoints at 3 widths with no layout overlap.

tasks.name: Charting primitive wrapper components
tasks.details: Sequence 5.3 (requires 5.2). Wrap the chosen chart library in a small internal API for LineChart, BarChart, DonutChart, Sparkline and Table, with consistent axes, units, tooltips, legend and a no-data overlay. Keep them dumb (props in, no fetching). Verification: a Storybook/gallery page renders each primitive with fixture data, and prop types are enforced.

tasks.name: Typed API client and data fetching hooks
tasks.details: Sequence 5.4 (requires 5.1 and the 4.2 contract). Generate or hand-write typed API client functions from the OpenAPI/types, add query hooks with caching, stale-while-revalidate, retries with backoff, request cancellation on unmount/filter change, and error normalization. Verification: hook tests with a mocked server cover success, error, retry and abort paths.

tasks.name: Shared loading, empty and error state components
tasks.details: Sequence 5.5 (requires 5.2). Build skeleton loaders, empty states with guidance, and error states with retry for use inside widget cards, plus a chart-specific "insufficient data" variant. Verification: a gallery demonstrates each state and every widget uses them instead of ad-hoc markup.

tasks.name: Customer analytics widgets
tasks.details: Sequence 5.6 (requires 5.3, 5.4, 5.5 and endpoint 4.3). Compose KPI cards (total customers, new in period, growth %), a new-customers trend line, and a segment/geography breakdown chart, each wired to its endpoint with loading/empty/error handling and a drill-through to the customer list. Verification: renders correct numbers against seeded API data and the component tests cover each state.

tasks.name: Operational health widgets (error rate, latency, throughput)
tasks.details: Sequence 5.7 (requires 5.3, 5.4, 5.5 and endpoint 4.4). Build the error-rate time series with threshold shading, latency percentile band chart (p50/p95/p99), throughput bar chart, and a service selector. Define what "good vs bad" looks like so the visuals are readable at a glance. Verification: numbers match seeded fixtures, gaps in data render as gaps, and threshold shading triggers correctly.

tasks.name: Top error signatures panel with drill-in
tasks.details: Sequence 5.8 (requires 5.6/5.7 patterns and endpoint 4.4). Build a ranked list of error fingerprints with count, first/last seen and trend sparkline; clicking one opens a detail drawer with the exemplar stack trace and a "view events" action that deep-links to the log explorer pre-filtered by that fingerprint. Verification: click-through carries the correct filter state into the explorer URL.

tasks.name: Log explorer table with filters and pagination
tasks.details: Sequence 5.9 (requires 5.4, 5.5 and endpoint 4.5). Build a virtualized log table (time, severity, service, route, message snippet) with filter controls, sort, page-size selection, infinite or cursor pagination, a row detail drawer showing the full redacted event, and copy/export of the current page. Verification: scrolling a 5k-row fixture stays responsive and filter changes reset pagination correctly.

tasks.name: Global time-range and filter control with URL state
tasks.details: Sequence 5.10 (requires 5.6-5.9). Build a shared filter bar (time-range presets plus custom range, service, environment and segment) whose state lives in the URL query string so views are shareable and survive refresh; every widget subscribes to the shared state and refetches coherently, with a single refresh action and a visible "data as of" timestamp. Verification: copying the URL into a fresh browser reproduces the identical filtered view, and changing the range updates all widgets exactly once (no duplicate fetches).

tasks.name: Accessibility and responsive cross-browser QA pass
tasks.details: Sequence 5.11 (last in this milestone, requires 5.10). Run automated axe/Lighthouse checks plus keyboard-only navigation, screen-reader labels on charts (text alternatives and data tables), focus order and contrast review; verify layouts at mobile/tablet/desktop widths and in Chrome, Safari and Firefox. Log and fix defects, then re-run the checks. Verification: zero critical axe violations, all interactive elements keyboard reachable, and a signed QA checklist per browser.

tasks.name: End-to-end test suite for critical journeys
tasks.details: Sequence 6.1 (requires 4.8 API and 5.11 UI QA). Automate the critical paths against a seeded environment: CSV upload to visible customer KPIs, log batch to visible error-rate/latency charts, log search drill-down, and auth/403 behaviour. Run in CI nightly and on release candidates with retries for flakiness and screenshots on failure. Verification: suite passes 3 consecutive runs and a deliberately broken selector fails it.

tasks.name: Pipeline performance and cost tuning
tasks.details: Sequence 6.2 (requires 2.7 and 3.7 pipelines). Benchmark both pipelines on production-sized inputs, identify the slowest stages, and tune (batched writes, partitioned reads, reduced shuffles, right-sized compute). Record runtime, memory and storage cost per run before/after against an agreed budget. Verification: a full day of logs and a 1M-row CSV each process within the agreed time budget, with the benchmark table committed.

tasks.name: Monitoring, alerting and data freshness checks
tasks.details: Sequence 6.3 (requires 2.7 and 3.7). Add metrics and alerts for pipeline success/failure, run duration, rows processed, reject rate spikes, rollup freshness (stale partition alarm), API error rate and p95 latency; include a health endpoint and a simple status page tile. Define alert thresholds and owners. Verification: a simulated failed run and a stale partition each fire the expected alert.

tasks.name: Operational runbooks and on-call documentation
tasks.details: Sequence 6.4 (requires 6.3). Write runbooks for the recurring incidents: failed CSV run, unparsed log spike, stale rollups, API latency regression, and bad deploy rollback. Document architecture overview, data-flow diagram, ownership, escalation path and known limitations; index everything from the README. Verification: someone outside the team follows the rollback runbook successfully in a staging drill.

tasks.name: Security, PII and access review sign-off
tasks.details: Sequence 6.5 (requires 3.8 redaction and 4.7 auth). Review what customer and log data lands where, confirm redaction and retention match policy, verify least-privilege roles, secret handling, dependency scanning and encryption in transit/at rest, and record findings with owners and remediation dates. Verification: no open critical or high findings, and the signed review is attached to the project.

tasks.name: Staged rollout and general availability sign-off
tasks.details: Sequence 6.6 (final task; requires 6.1-6.5). Deploy to staging, run a pilot with a small user group for one week collecting feedback and defects, then ramp to all users with a rollback switch ready. Produce the launch checklist (data backfilled, alerts live, runbooks published, owners assigned) and get stakeholder sign-off. Verification: pilot feedback triaged, checklist fully ticked, and GA announced with metrics being watched.
